title: Compressible Euler equations, symmetric hyperbolic systems and maximal developments
summary: The barotropic and full compressible Euler systems with a general equation of state on the Galilean carrier ℝ × ℝⁿ (partially periodic carriers as Λ-periodic lifts); quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic systems with the Euler symmetrisers; the acoustical form, Lipschitz causal curves of sound-cone fields and future domains of dependence; Hᵏ_Λ calculus (Gagliardo–Nirenberg, Moser, mollifiers); Friedrichs energy estimates; local uniqueness on lenses and on domains of dependence; local well-posedness in Hᵏ_Λ, k > n/2 + 1; developments, maximal common developments, maximal developments (non-unique in general, with an explicit counterexample; unique when the data extend to a classical solution on the whole future half-space), existence of developments, and nullity of the regular boundary of every maximal development.

layers.title: Equations of state and the Euler systems

targets.name: CompressibleEuler.BarotropicEOS
targets.statement: A barotropic equation of state is an open interval I ⊆ (0,∞) and p : ℝ → ℝ smooth on I with p′ > 0 on I; its sound speed is c(ρ) = √(p′ ρ). A (full) equation of state is an open 𝒪 ⊆ (0,∞) × ℝ and P smooth on 𝒪 with ∂_ρP > 0 on 𝒪; its sound speed is √(∂_ρP).
hypotheses: for the full law: 𝒪 open in (0,∞) × ℝ, P smooth on 𝒪, ∂_ρP > 0

layers.title: Symmetric hyperbolic systems and the Euler symmetrisers

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.QuasilinearSystem
targets.statement: A quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system of size N in n space dimensions: an open G ⊆ ℝ^N, smooth A⁰,…,Aⁿ : G → symmetric N×N real matrices with A⁰(U) positive definite for all U ∈ G, and smooth F : G → ℝ^N. A classical solution on D is a C¹ map U : D → G with A⁰(U)∂_tU + Σᵢ Aⁱ(U)∂ᵢU = F(U). The symbol is σ(U;ζ) = ζ₀A⁰(U) + Σ ζᵢAⁱ(U); a round cone (c, w), c > 0, dominates at U when σ(U;ζ) is positive semidefinite for every ζ with ζ₀ + w·ζ′ ≥ c|ζ′|.

locator.where: Ch. 2, §2.1; Friedrichs1954 pp. 345–392; Dafermos2016 Ch. V, §5.1; Christodoulou2019 lines 124–126

api.name: symbol_dt
api.statement: σ(U; dt) = A⁰(U) is positive definite and σ is linear in ζ

api.name: dominates_mono
api.statement: if (c,w) dominates at U and c′ ≥ c + |w′ − w| then (c′,w′) dominates at U

api.name: exists_maxSpeed

api.name: isClosed_dominates

api.name: exists_dominatingConeMap

api.name: ofSymmetriser
api.statement: multiplying ∂_tU + Mⁱ(U)∂ᵢU = f(U) by a smooth positive definite S with S Mⁱ symmetric gives a system with the same C¹ solutions

tests.statement: n = 1, Λ = 2πℤ, k = 1: cos x has TauCeti.CircleSobolev 1 ℂ norm² 2 and H¹_Λ norm² 2π; the constant 1 has 1 and 2π; ratios π and 2π differ, so equivalent but not proportional

tests.name: wkp_norm_n1
tests.statement: n = 1, k = 2, u = e^{−x²}: both squared norms are √(π/2) + √(π/2) + 3√(π/2) = 5√(π/2); equality holds at every order in dimension one

targets.name: PeriodicSobolev.embedding
targets.statement: If 2k > n + 2j, every u ∈ Hᵏ_Λ has a Cʲ representative with sup_{|α|≤j}‖∂^αu‖_∞ ≤ C‖u‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}, derivatives tending to 0 orthogonally to span Λ; for k ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ j ≤ k, ‖u‖_{Hʲ_Λ} ≤ C‖u‖^{1−j/k}_{L²_Λ}‖u‖^{j/k}_{Hᵏ_Λ} (k = 0 is the identity on L²_Λ); if u_m → u in L²_Λ with ‖u_m‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} ≤ M then u ∈ Hᵏ_Λ with norm ≤ M.
hypotheses: k ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ j ≤ k for interpolation (k = 0: identity)

tests.name: critical_log
tests.statement: n = 2, k = 1: cut-off log log(1 + 1/|x|) ∈ H¹ is unbounded

tests.name: interpolation_exponents
tests.statement: j=1, k=2, e^{−x²}: ‖u‖²_{H¹} = 2√(π/2) ≤ √5·√(π/2); exponents (2/3,1/3) refuted by dilation (λ^{1/2} versus λ^{1/6})

targets.name: PeriodicSobolev.gagliardoNirenberg
targets.statement: For u ∈ L^∞ ∩ Hᵏ_Λ, k ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ k: ‖Dⁱu‖_{L^{2k/i}_Λ} ≤ C‖u‖_∞^{1−i/k}‖u‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}^{i/k} (homogeneous form with ‖Dᵏu‖ for Λ = 0); i = 0 is the L^∞ norm itself and k = 0 has no positive order.

locator.where: line 318, Lecture II, Theorem, inequality (2.2), p. 125

tests.name: scaling
tests.statement: homogeneous Λ = 0 form: under u(λx) both ‖Dⁱu‖_{L^{2k/i}} and ‖u‖_∞^{1−i/k}‖Dᵏu‖_{L²}^{i/k} scale as λ^{i − ni/(2k)}; the wrong L^{k/i} left side scales as λ^{i − ni/k}, ratio λ^{−ni/(2k)}, unbounded as λ → 0 (not as λ → ∞); n = 1, k = 2, i = 1: wrong side λ^{1/2}, right side λ^{3/4}, ratio 2 at λ = 1/16 and 1/2 at λ = 16

tests.name: order_zero_exponents
tests.statement: k = i = 0: the exponents 2k/i and i/k are 0/0, so the statement starts at k ≥ 1, i ≥ 1; at k = i = 1 it reads ‖Du‖ ≤ C‖u‖_{H¹_Λ}, true with C = 1

targets.name: PeriodicSobolev.moser_product_commutator
targets.statement: For |α| ≤ k: ‖∂^α(fg)‖ ≤ C(‖f‖_∞‖g‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} + ‖f‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}‖g‖_∞); Hᵏ_Λ is an algebra for 2k > n; for 1 ≤ |α| ≤ k: ‖∂^α(fg) − f∂^αg‖ ≤ C(‖∇f‖_∞‖g‖_{Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ} + ‖∇f‖_{Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ}‖g‖_∞).

locator.where: Ch. 2, §2.1 (Moser product and commutator estimates); the product bound is derived here from 4.3, the Leibniz rule and Hölder's inequality

tests.name: L2_not_algebra
tests.statement: |x|^{−n/3} on the unit ball is in L² but its square is not

targets.name: PeriodicSobolev.moser_composition
targets.statement: For Φ smooth on open G ⊆ ℝ^N, compact K ⊆ G, Ū ∈ K and u with values in K and u − Ū ∈ Hᵏ_Λ: Φ(u) − Φ(Ū) ∈ Hᵏ_Λ with ‖Φ(u) − Φ(Ū)‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} ≤ C‖u − Ū‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}; for Λ = 0 and k ≥ 1, ‖DᵏΦ(u)‖_{L²} ≤ C‖Dᵏu‖_{L²}; and u ↦ Φ(u) is continuous in Hᵏ_Λ. C depends on n, k, Λ, K, a δ > 0 with the closed δ-neighbourhood K_δ ⊆ G, and the derivatives of Φ of order ≤ max(1, k) on K_δ; at order 0 it is the secant bound |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ max(sup_{K_δ}|DΦ|, 2δ⁻¹ sup_K|Φ|)|a − b| for a, b ∈ K.
hypotheses: values of u in compact K
δ > 0 with closed δ-neighbourhood K_δ of K contained in G

tests.name: order_zero_uncentred
tests.statement: Λ = 0, K = {0}, u = Ū = 0, Φ ≡ 1, k = 0: the uncentred bound ‖Φ(u)‖_{L²} ≤ C‖u‖_{L²} has sides ∞ and 0; the centred bound gives 0 ≤ 0

tests.name: order_zero_lipschitz
tests.statement: Λ = 0, n = N = 1, K = [0,1], Ū = 0, Φ_m(s) = sin(ms), u_m = m⁻¹1_{[0,1]}: sup_K|Φ_m| = 1 (m ≥ 2), ‖u_m‖ = 1/m, ‖Φ_m(u_m) − Φ_m(0)‖ = sin 1 ≈ 0.8415, so the k = 0 constant is ≥ m sin 1 and no bound by sup_K|Φ| alone exists; with Lip Φ_m = m the bound reads sin 1 ≤ 1

targets.name: PeriodicSobolev.mollify
targets.statement: For ε > 0, J_εu = φ_ε ⋆ u with φ ∈ C_c^∞(E) even, nonnegative, ∫φ = 1, φ_ε = ε^{−n}φ(·/ε).
hypotheses: φ even, nonnegative, compactly supported, smooth, ∫φ = 1

api.name: bounds
api.statement: preserves Λ-periodicity; ‖J_εu‖_{Hᵏ} ≤ ‖u‖_{Hᵏ}; symmetric for the L²_Λ pairing; commutes with ∂ᵢ; J_εu → u in Hᵏ_Λ. Owned here for every admissible kernel and every Λ: J_εu = ∫φ(y)τ_{−εy}u dy as a Bochner integral of the translates TauCeti.Wkp.translate (continuous in y by TauCeti.Wkp.continuous_translate, isometric by TauCeti.Wkp.norm_translate / translateLIE); contraction from φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1 (Young coordinatewise in the multi-index norm); commutation from TauCeti.Wkp.lowerOrder_translate and iteratedGradient_translate; strong convergence by dominated convergence of ‖τ_{−εy}u − u‖ ≤ 2‖u‖. For Λ = 0 and a normalised ContDiffBump kernel these are TauCeti.Wkp.norm_normedBumpL_le_one, lowerOrder_normedBumpL, iteratedGradient_normedBumpL and tendsto_normedBumpL at p = 2, which the route recovers

api.name: gain_loss
api.statement: for every ε > 0, ‖J_εu‖_{Hᵏ⁺¹} ≤ C(1 + ε^{−1})‖u‖_{Hᵏ}, hence ≤ 2Cε^{−1}‖u‖_{Hᵏ} for 0 < ε ≤ 1; for k ≥ 1 and every ε > 0, ‖J_εu − u‖_{Hᵏ⁻¹} ≤ Cε‖u‖_{Hᵏ}

api.name: friedrichs_lemma
api.statement: for a bounded, Lipschitz and Λ-periodic (any bounded Lipschitz a when Λ = 0): ‖J_ε(a∂ᵢu) − a∂ᵢJ_εu‖_{L²_Λ} ≤ C(‖a‖_∞ + Lip a)‖u‖_{L²_Λ} for every ε > 0, tending to 0 strongly as ε → 0

tests.name: constants
tests.statement: J_ε fixes constants; the scaling φ(·/ε) would multiply them by εⁿ

tests.name: cosine
tests.statement: J_ε cos(mx) = φ̂(εm)cos(mx); the ε^{−1} gain is attained at m ≈ 1/ε

tests.name: linear_coefficient
tests.statement: for a = x on ℝ the commutator is ψ′ ⋆ u with ‖ψ′‖_{L¹} = ∫|φ + wφ′| independent of ε

tests.name: loss_needs_k_ge_one
tests.statement: k = 0: ‖J_ε cos(mx) − cos(mx)‖₂ = |1 − φ̂(εm)|‖cos(mx)‖₂ → ‖cos(mx)‖₂ as m → ∞, exceeding Cε‖cos(mx)‖₂ once Cε < 1; for k = 1 the bound holds since |1 − φ̂(η)| ≤ |η|∫|y|φ

tests.name: gain_large_eps
tests.statement: Λ = 2πℤ, u = 1: J_εu = 1 and ‖1‖_{Hᵏ⁺¹_Λ} = ‖1‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} = √(2π); a bound Cε^{−1} for all ε > 0 fails at ε = 2C, while 1 ≤ C(1 + ε^{−1}) holds for C ≥ 1

tests.name: nonperiodic_coefficient
tests.statement: Λ = 2πℤ, u = sin x, a = sin(x/2): the commutator ½[(φ̂(3ε/2) − φ̂(ε))sin(3x/2) − (φ̂(ε/2) − φ̂(ε))sin(x/2)] equals μ₂ε²/8 + o(ε²) at x = π and its negative at 3π, so it is not in L²_Λ; a = sin x gives a periodic commutator, constant a gives 0

tests.name: two_bump_kernel
tests.statement: φ(x) = (η(x−2) + η(x+2))/2 with η even, nonnegative, ∫η = 1, supp η ⊆ (−1/4,1/4) is admissible (even, ∫φ = 1) with φ(0) = 0, while every normalised ContDiffBump is positive at 0, so J_ε is not a TauCeti.Wkp.normedBumpL; J_εu = ½(τ_{2ε} + τ_{−2ε})(η_ε ⋆ u) is still a contraction and ∫φ(y)‖τ_{−εy}u − u‖ → 0

layers.title: Energy estimates for linear symmetric hyperbolic systems

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.LinearOperator
targets.statement: A linear symmetric hyperbolic operator LW = A⁰∂_tW + Σᵢ Aⁱ∂ᵢW + BW on [0,T] × E with Λ-periodic coefficients and symmetric values: A⁰ bounded, C¹ with bounded first derivatives, A⁰ ≥ λ₀I (λ₀ > 0); Aⁱ bounded, continuous, with bounded continuous spatial derivatives (no time derivative of Aⁱ enters); B continuous bounded; its energy E(t) = ∫_F ⟨A⁰W, W⟩ (finite and comparable to ‖W‖²_{L²_Λ} because A⁰ is bounded).
hypotheses: A⁰ bounded, C¹ with bounded first derivatives
Aⁱ bounded, continuous, with bounded continuous spatial derivatives

api.name: energy_equiv
api.statement: λ₀‖W‖² ≤ E ≤ sup‖A⁰‖‖W‖²

api.name: time_reverse
api.statement: t ↦ T − t gives a linear symmetric hyperbolic operator with A⁰ unchanged

tests.name: transport
tests.statement: A⁰ = 1, A¹ = a, B = 0: W = W₀(x − at), E constant

tests.name: damping_sign
tests.statement: A⁰ = I, Aⁱ = 0, B = bI: E(t) = e^{−2bt}E(0); a sign error gives e^{2bt}

tests.name: jordan_block
tests.statement: A¹ = [[0,1],[0,0]]: ‖W(t)‖ grows like t‖f′‖, no L² estimate

tests.name: unbounded_A0
tests.statement: n = N = 1, Λ = 0, A⁰ = √(1+x²) (A⁰ ≥ 1, |∂ₓA⁰| ≤ 1), A¹ = B = 0, W = (1+x²)^{−1/2}: LW = 0, ‖W‖² = π, ‖∂ₓW‖² = π/8, but ∫_{−R}^{R}A⁰W² = 2 asinh R → ∞; excluded by the bound on A⁰; with A⁰ = 1, E = π and both sides of the identity are 0

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.LinearOperator.energy_identity
targets.statement: For W ∈ C¹([0,T];L²_Λ) ∩ C([0,T];H¹_Λ): dE/dt = ∫_F⟨(∂_tA⁰ + Σ∂ᵢAⁱ − B − Bᵀ)W,W⟩ + 2∫_F⟨LW,W⟩, and ‖W(t)‖ ≤ Ce^{Ct}(‖W(0)‖ + ∫₀ᵗ‖LW‖) with C depending on λ₀, sup‖A⁰‖, sup|∂_tA⁰|, sup|∂ᵢAⁱ| and sup‖B‖, all finite by the hypotheses of 5.1.
hypotheses: L as in 5.1: A⁰ bounded, C¹ with bounded first derivatives, A⁰ ≥ λ₀I; Aⁱ bounded with bounded spatial derivatives; B continuous and bounded

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.weighted_energy
targets.statement: If χ ≥ 0 is Lipschitz and Λ-periodic with {χ > 0} relatively compact modulo Λ in [0,T] × E, W is Λ-periodic and W and the coefficients of L are C¹ on a relatively open set containing the closure of {χ > 0}, ∂_tχA⁰ + Σ∂ᵢχAⁱ ≤ 0 a.e. on {χ > 0} and |LW| ≤ C₁|W| there, then E_χ(t) = ∫_Fχ⟨A⁰W,W⟩ is finite, Lipschitz in t, and E_χ(t) ≤ e^{Ct}E_χ(0).
hypotheses: W Λ-periodic; W and the coefficients C¹ on a relatively open set containing the closure of {χ > 0}

tests.name: steep_cone_fails
tests.statement: transport a = 1, χ = (1 − |x| − t/2)₊ is not monotone and u = f(x − t) with supp f ⊆ (−2,−1) has E_χ(0) = 0 < E_χ(0.9)

tests.name: sound_cone_equality
tests.statement: Euler constant state: χ = (R − |x − tv₀| − c₀t)₊ gives ∂_tχ + v₀·∇χ + c₀|∇χ| = 0

tests.name: boundary_regularity
tests.statement: Λ = 0, L = ∂_t, χ = (1 − |x|)₊, W = (1 − x)^{−1} on (−1,1): W is C¹ on {χ > 0}, LW = 0, σ(dχ) = 0, but ∫₀¹ χW² = ∫₀¹ (1 − x)^{−1} = ∞; W is not C¹ near the closure, which the hypothesis demands

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.Hk_estimate
targets.statement: For U with values in compact K, U − Ū ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ) ∩ C¹([0,T];Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ), 2k > n + 2, and W in the same class with A⁰(U)∂_tW + ΣAⁱ(U)∂ᵢW = f, f ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ): E_k is C¹ and dE_k/dt ≤ C(1 + ‖∂_tU‖_∞ + ‖U − Ū‖_{Hᵏ_Λ})E_k + C(1 + ‖U − Ū‖_{Hᵏ_Λ})E_k^{1/2}‖f‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}, C depending only on K, the system, n, k and Λ; when U solves the system with F(Ū) = 0, d/dt E_k(U − Ū) ≤ C(1 + ‖∇U‖_∞)E_k(U − Ū). For a classical solution with values in K, ‖∂_tU‖_∞ ≤ C(‖F(U)‖_∞ + ‖∇U‖_∞) ≤ C(1 + ‖∇U‖_∞), and ≤ C‖∇U‖_∞ when F = 0.
hypotheses: values of U in compact K ⊆ G
constants depend on K, the system, n, k, Λ only; the forcing coefficient also on ‖U − Ū‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}

tests.name: burgers_tame
tests.statement: Burgers: d/dt‖u‖² = 0 and d/dt‖u_x‖² = −∫u_x³ ≤ ‖u_x‖_∞‖u_x‖²

tests.name: forcing_coefficient
tests.statement: Λ = 2πℤ, k = 2, A⁰(u) = 1/(2 + u), A¹ = 0, K = [−1,1], Ū = 0, U = sin(mx), f = 1, W = (δ + t)(2 + sin(mx)): E₂ = (δ + t)²S_m, S_m ≥ πm⁴/3; a forcing coefficient C₁ depending on K alone needs C₁ ≥ √(2/3)m² for every m; C(1 + ‖sin(mx)‖_{H²}) ~ m² suffices

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.linear_existence
targets.statement: For coefficients with A^μ − Ā^μ, B ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ), A⁰ − Ā⁰ ∈ C¹([0,T];Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ) (so ∂_tA⁰ is bounded, 2(k−1) > n), A⁰ ≥ λ₀I, 2k > n + 2, W₀ ∈ Hᵏ_Λ and f ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ) there is a unique W ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ) ∩ C¹([0,T];Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ) with LW = f, W(0) = W₀, obeying the estimate dE_k/dt ≤ C E_k + C E_k^{1/2}‖f‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} of 5.3 with C depending on n, N, k, Λ, λ₀, the constant matrices Ā⁰, …, Āⁿ (spatial ones included), sup_t ‖∂_tA⁰‖_∞, sup_t ‖A^μ − Ā^μ‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} and sup_t ‖B‖_{Hᵏ_Λ}.

locator.where: Ch. 2, §2.1 (linear existence); Kato1975 Theorem I; LukNotes line 1158, Theorem 5.3

tests.name: background_speed
tests.statement: Λ = 2πℤ, k = 2, A⁰ = e^{sin x}, A¹ = M, B = f = 0, W(0) = sin x + sin 2x: E₂′(0) = 22πM, E₂(0) ≤ 24eπ, while λ₀ = e^{−1}, ∂_tA⁰ = 0, A^μ − Ā^μ do not depend on M; C must depend on |Ā¹|

layers.title: Local uniqueness and domains of dependence

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.LensFunction
targets.statement: A lens function on [t₁,t₂] × E is a Lipschitz Λ-periodic φ with {φ > 0} relatively compact modulo Λ in [t₁,t₂] × E; its lens L_φ = {φ > 0}, its base L_φ ∩ Σ_{t₁}; φ is spacelike for a solution U when σ(U; dφ) ≤ 0 a.e. on L_φ (for Euler: ∂_tφ + v·∇φ + c|∇φ| ≤ 0).

api.name: min
api.statement: the minimum (intersection) and the maximum (union) of two lens functions spacelike for U are lens functions spacelike for U

api.name: movingCone
api.statement: the periodised moving cone max_{λ∈Λ}(R − |x − λ − x₀ − (t−t₁)w| − M(t−t₁)) is a lens function (Lipschitz, Λ-periodic, lens inside the Λ-translates of [t₁,t₂] × B(x₀, R + |w|(t₂ − t₁)), hence relatively compact modulo Λ; the single cone when Λ = 0; disjoint translates when 2R is below the least nonzero norm of Λ), spacelike for U₁ when (M,w) dominates at U₁ on the lens, since a.e. its differential is that of a term attaining the maximum

tests.name: sound_cone_null
tests.statement: constant Euler state: R − |x − tv₀| − c₀t is spacelike with equality

tests.name: static_vs_moving
tests.statement: n = 1, v₀ = 3, c₀ = 1: static cone needs M ≥ 4, moving cone (w = 3) M ≥ 1

tests.name: steep_lens
tests.statement: transport a = 1, φ = 1 − |x| − t/2 is not spacelike for x < 0

tests.name: single_cone_not_periodic
tests.statement: n = 1, Λ = 2πℤ, t = t₁: the single cone takes R at x₀ and R − 2π at x₀ + 2π, so it is not Λ-periodic; its periodisation takes R at both

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.eq_on_lens
targets.statement: If U₁, U₂ are Λ-periodic classical solutions of the same quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system on a Λ-invariant relatively open set containing the closure of L_φ, φ is spacelike for U₁, and U₁ = U₂ on the base, then U₁ = U₂ on L_φ.
hypotheses: U₁, U₂ Λ-periodic (no condition for Λ = 0)
φ spacelike for U₁ (only U₁'s cones)

locator.where: Ch. 2, §2.3; LukNotes line 724, Proposition 4.4; EperonReallSbierski2019 line 1178, Proposition 4.63; BarGinouxPfaffle2007 lines 3664–3668

tests.name: nonperiodic_solutions
tests.statement: Λ = ℤ, φ = 1 − t on [0,2] × ℝ (spacelike for every solution); the system A⁰ = I, A¹(u,z) = diag(z², 0) has solutions (0, x) and (g(t + 1/x)·1_{x<0}, x), g supported in (1/2,1), equal at t = 0 and different at (0.9, −1/0.3); neither is ℤ-periodic

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.eq_on_causalPast
targets.statement: Given a continuous dominating cone map κ, a domain D, a classical solution U₁ on D with field κ ∘ U₁, S ⊆ D relatively open in Σ_{t₀}, a relatively open O ⊆ H_{t₀} and a classical solution U₂ on O with U₁ = U₂ on S ∩ O: for p ∈ D⁺_D(S) with J⁻_D(p) ⊆ O, U₁ = U₂ on J⁻_D(p) (the lenses of the route are moving cones of 6.1 with Λ = 0).
hypotheses: κ continuous and dominating at every state

tests.name: constant_state
tests.statement: p = ρ²/2, constant (1,0), data agreeing on (−2,2): agreement on {|x| < 2 − t}, e.g. at (1/2,1.4)

tests.name: past_not_contained
tests.statement: in the counter-flow of 8.2.4 the solutions agree on S and differ at (2,0), where J⁻ of one leaves the other domain

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.eq_on_slab
targets.statement: Two classical solutions on [t₀,t₁) × E with the same data on Σ_{t₀} and bounded cone fields on each [t₀,t₂] × E agree.
hypotheses: bounded cone fields on compact time ranges

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.localWellPosedness
targets.statement: For a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system, Ū ∈ G with F(Ū) = 0, a period group Λ, 2k > n + 2, a compact K ⊆ G and M > 0, there are T(M,K) > 0 and R(M,K) such that every U₀ with U₀ − Ū ∈ Hᵏ_Λ, ‖U₀ − Ū‖ ≤ M and U₀(E) ⊆ K has a unique Λ-periodic classical solution U on [0,T] × E with U − Ū ∈ C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ) ∩ C¹([0,T];Hᵏ⁻¹_Λ) and ‖U(t) − Ū‖_{Hᵏ_Λ} ≤ R on [0,T]; it is unique among classical solutions with bounded cone fields, depends continuously on the data in C([0,T];Hᵏ_Λ), and persists in Hᵏ′_Λ for k′ > k on the same maximal interval.

locator.where: Theorem I; Majda1984 Ch. 2, Theorem 2.1; Dafermos2016 Ch. V, Theorem 5.1.1; LukNotes line 1239, Theorem 6.1

tests.name: source_at_infinity
tests.statement: F ≡ 1, Ū = 0: u = u₀ + t leaves Ū + L² for t > 0, so F(Ū) = 0 is needed

tests.name: constant_data
tests.statement: U₀ ≡ Ū gives the constant solution with T* = ∞

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.continuation
targets.statement: If the maximal time T* is finite then ∫₀^{T*}‖∇U(t)‖_∞dt = ∞ or the closure of U([0,T*) × E) is not a compact subset of G.

targets.name: CompressibleEuler.localWellPosedness
targets.statement: For a barotropic law (I,p), a period group Λ, 2k > n + 2, a background (ρ₀,v₀) ∈ I × E and data with ρ̄ − ρ₀, v̄ − v₀ ∈ Hᵏ_Λ and ρ_* ≤ ρ̄ ≤ ρ^* for [ρ_*,ρ^*] ⊆ I: there are T > 0 and a unique Λ-periodic classical solution on [t₀, t₀+T] × E with (ρ − ρ₀, v − v₀) ∈ C(Hᵏ_Λ) and ρ ≥ ρ_*/2, depending continuously on the data; if the maximal time is finite then ∫‖∇(ρ,v)‖_∞ = ∞ or the closure of the range of ρ is not compact in I. The full system is analogous with s̄ − s₀ ∈ Hᵏ_Λ and (ρ̄,s̄) in a compact subset of 𝒪.

locator.where: lines 172–179; ChristodoulouMiao2014 lines 866–868; LuoYu2023a lines 82–95; Majda1984 Ch. 2

tests.name: cylinder_symmetry
tests.statement: on Λ_cyl, n = 2, data independent of x² give solutions independent of x²

tests.name: sobolev_threshold
tests.statement: n = 3: k = 3 gives 2k = 6 > 5 (the H³ setting of Abbrescia–Speck); k = 2 gives 4 < 5 and is excluded

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.QuasilinearSystem.sourceSwitched
targets.statement: For a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system (G, A⁰, …, Aⁿ, F), the source-switched system on G × ℝ with states (U, a), coefficient matrices diag(A⁰(U), 1), diag(Aⁱ(U), 0) and source (aF(U), 0).
hypotheses: (G, A^μ, F) quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system

locator.where: Theorem I (the uniformly local existence theorem that 7.3 states); the switching construction is not taken from it

api.name: isSymmetricHyperbolic

targets.name: SymmetricHyperbolic.localWellPosedness_uniformlyLocal
targets.statement: Let (G, A^μ, F) be a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system with arbitrary smooth F, Ū ∈ G, K ⊆ G compact with [Ū,U] ⊆ G for U ∈ K, 2k > n + 2, M > 0, χ ∈ C_c^∞(E) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on the unit ball. There is T > 0 (depending on the system, n, k, χ, Ū, K, M) such that every U₀ : E → K with U₀ − Ū ∈ Hᵏ_loc and sup_y‖χ(·−y)(U₀ − Ū)‖_{Hᵏ(E)} ≤ M has a unique classical solution on [0,T] × E with U(0) = U₀; its values lie in a compact subset of G depending on G, Ū, K, its uniformly local Hᵏ norm is bounded on [0,T], and it commutes with translations fixing U₀, so periodic data give periodic solutions. Route: 7.1 (Λ = 0) for the source-switched system 7.3.1 at the equilibrium (Ū,0) with data (Ū + χ(·−y)(U₀ − Ū), χ(·−y)), a compact neighbourhood K₁ ⊆ G of the segment hull for a uniform short time, cones of speed m = sup_{K₁} of the maximal speed, gluing by 6.2, uniqueness by 6.2 with 3.3.3.
hypotheses: quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system with smooth F (F(Ū) = 0 not assumed)
χ ∈ C_c^∞(E), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on the unit ball
U₀(E) ⊆ K, U₀ − Ū ∈ Hᵏ_loc, uniformly local Hᵏ bound M
